In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ρ ( 700 ) 0 production is not modified in the medium, and the observed modification in the ρ (770)0 production is consistent with the effect of the initial-state nuclear effects, which are also responsible for the Cronin enhancement of π ± production in the same collisions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ρ 0 meson is suppressed relative to the expectation from a superposition of nucleon-nucleon collisions at the measured multiplicity.
the ρ 0 production is consistent with the binary collision scaling in the intermediate p T region, and is suppressed in the low p T region.

ρ 0 production in the hadronic matter is not modified significantly in Cu+Cu at s N N < 62.4, while the ρ 0 suppression at s N N ≥ 200 GeV is due to the strong final-state interaction with the produced hadron gas, which is similar to that observed in Pb+Pb collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ρ 0 yield in central Cu+Cu collisions is suppressed by a factor of 2-3 at s N N= 62.4 and 200 GeV relative to the yield in pp collisions scaled by the number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions.
the ρ 0 meson production is suppressed in the most central 0-5% Cu+Cu collisions, and the magnitude of this suppression is consistent with the one observed in Au+Au collisions.
the ρ 0 production is consistent with a scenario where the ρ  is produced early, before the medium is formed, and subsequently decays in vacuum.
